text:
sara: Quick notes from today's thin-queue-proxy experiment (summary + triage). Spun up a lightweight proxy in front of the batcher to centralize eviction decisions and soften hot-tenant bursts.

matt: Thin queue proxy == extra hop that holds short-lived request metadata? can you sketch behaviour?

sara: Yep — it keeps a tiny in-memory queue, annotates requests with cost hints, and runs a cheap eviction/ordering pass before sending to the continuous batcher. Idea: move most of the eviction churn out of the hot batcher code path.

leo: Any perf numbers? we worry about added hop overhead.

sara: Short numbers from 30m A/B:
- baseline (no proxy): p50 18ms, p95 120ms, p99 220ms
- proxy enabled: p50 21ms, p95 110ms, p99 190ms
Throughput ~ unchanged. Observed ~40% fewer eviction-triggered batch restarts.

matt: So p50 +3ms but p99 improves. Sounds promising if tail stabilizes. Do you have traces to show where the p99 delta comes from?

sara: Traces show fewer kernel-lock/queue-scan spikes in batcher. Proxy does a best-effort cheap check and drops or reorders worst offenders earlier instead of letting batcher discover and evict mid-flight.

nina: How does this affect tenant fairness? policy matters a lot here — cheap LRU might favor many small requests over a single large tenant job.

sara: Agreed. Current experiment used cost-aware LRU with soft quotas per tenant. Config sketch:
```yaml
proxy:
  backlog_limit: 8000
  admission_window_ms: 5
  eviction_policy: cost_aware_lru
  tenant_soft_quota_tokens: 10000
```
Eviction decision pseudocode: `if tenant_tokens > soft_quota -> mark as candidate_for_eviction(priority=tenant_overuse)` else `mark by cost_per_token`

leo: Does proxy need per-tenant state? that increases memory and GC risk.

sara: We keep a compact approximate counter (small LFU sketch) to avoid per-request allocations. State per-tenant is optional; default uses hop-by-hop hints without durable counters. Dedicated infra can enable stronger tracking.

matt: What about correctness / ordering? reordering might break some ordering guarantees for multi-call flows.

sara: Good call — we only reorder within a small admission window (<=5ms) and don't touch requests that declare ordering constraints (client flag `x-ordering=seq`). We added a simple opt-out header.

nina: Telemetry we should add before wider rollout: `proxy_evicted_reason`, `upstream_queue_len`, `tenant_soft_quota_exceeded`, and link to batcher`eviction_origin`.

sara: Already added those tags in the run. Quick list for postmortem metrics:
- proxy.evictions.count
- proxy.evictions.by_reason
- batcher.restart.count (eviction-triggered)
- p50/p95/p99 per-tenant

leo: Are we planning to expose this as an opt-in flag per-customer? feels risky to flip globally.

sara: Plan A: Dedicated customers toggle via config. Plan B: Hosted rollouts behind feature flag + telemetry alerting that auto-rolls-back if batcher.restart.count increases >10% vs baseline.

matt: Implementation questions: do we implement proxy as a sidecar per-batcher or as a shared service?

sara: Sidecar preferred for locality and simpler failure modes. Shared service reduces memory but increases network hop variability. Sidecar kept latency bounded in our test.

nina: Edge cases: what if proxy crashes/ozone? we need a fast passthrough fallback so gateway can bypass proxy immediately.

sara: Yes fallback = gateway detects missing health ping -> switch to bypass mode. ci-bot posted the deploy log for today's experiment: `ci-bot: deploy thin-queue-proxy v0.1 -> green (15m)`

matt: Next steps?

sara: Short action list: 
1) Add the telemetry keys nina listed (owner: nina) 
2) Add opt-out header to SDK (owner: matt) 
3) Harden sidecar memory (approx counters + bounded eviction table) (owner: leo) 
4) Draft rollout playbook with auto-rollback triggers + runbook (owner: sara)

leo: +1 to owners. I'll start a tiny design doc on the memory plan and a simulation to validate fairness knobs.

nina: I'll wire the telemetry and a dashboard for evictions.

matt: I'll add SDK header and a quick sample showing `x-ordering=seq` opt-out.

sara: Thanks all. TL;DR: proxy adds tiny p50 overhead, reduces tail by ~30-40% in prelims, needs fairness tuning + telemetry before ramp. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: deploy log: thin-queue-proxy experiment ended — artifacts uploaded to s3://ci-artifacts/thin-queue/6182739999/
